wiki-iran.standing: How many people open the Wikipedia article on Iran each day. It jumps when the country is at the centre of a war, a negotiation or a crisis, so the spikes mark the days the wider world went looking for background.
wiki-iran.recent: Iran's Revolutionary Guards say 3 tankers hit mines in Hormuz, and Rezaei tied reopening to seven conditions; Ghalibaf claims an Oman lane deal Muscat hasn't confirmed. Abroad, Bessent moved onto a military base, the US charged three alleged Iran-backed operatives, and France blamed the Guards for hacking 700 supermarkets.

brent.standing: The price of a barrel of North Sea crude, and the reference against which most of the world's internationally traded oil is priced. Petrol, diesel and jet fuel costs follow it, and so do the budgets of oil-exporting states.
brent.recent: The Hormuz closure in the Iran war cut Asia off from Gulf barrels, and the price has come off as supply found other routes: Saudi Arabia reported output up 26% in October and China's crude imports hit a seven-month high. The squeeze moved east instead, with sanctioned Russian ESPO crude now selling above Brent as China and India bid for it.

wti.standing: West Texas Intermediate: the price of a barrel of light, sweet crude delivered at Cushing, Oklahoma, and the benchmark for American oil. US petrol and diesel prices follow it, and so do shale drillers' budgets.
wti.recent: The Iran war and the closure of Hormuz kept crude dear, with Iran's media saying it targeted 11 tankers in 10 days. The November slide followed Trump calling a new Iran offensive 'highly unlikely', and Saudi Arabia reporting October output up 26%, even as an attack set its East-West pipeline ablaze.

natgas-hh.standing: The futures price of gas delivered at Henry Hub in Louisiana, the benchmark for the American market. It moves on weather, storage and LNG exports, and sets what US power plants and households pay for heat and electricity.
natgas-hh.recent: The pull on American gas came from the Gulf. With Hormuz disrupted, QatarEnergy agreed to buy up to 3 million tonnes of US liquefied natural gas a year, and an attack struck Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline, the route built to carry Gulf energy around the strait.

wheat.standing: The export price of a tonne of US hard red winter wheat loaded at the Gulf of Mexico, a reference for bread wheat worldwide. Importers from Egypt to Indonesia buy against it, and bread subsidy budgets strain when it rises.
wheat.recent: Ukraine's grain corridor came back into play: Zelensky said Turkey would help restore it, and Rubio floated a Black Sea ceasefire. Israel's war left 24% of Lebanon's wheatland fallow, and Punjab and Sindh moved to cut flour prices. All of it came after this reading, so none of it explains the rise.

rice.standing: The export price of a tonne of Thai white rice, the benchmark much of Asia's and Africa's import trade is priced against. Rice is the staple for about half the world, so a move here reaches household food budgets directly.

copper.standing: The price of a tonne of refined copper, the metal in every wire, motor and transformer. Demand follows construction and electrification, and supply rests on a handful of mines in Chile, Peru and the Congo.
copper.recent: Chinese buyers paid a record $200-plus a ton over London prices at Shanghai on AI demand; then fears of an AI backlash took copper to $13,778, its lowest since July. Codelco signed Adani to finance Kaburkaala in Chile for future supply to its Mundra smelter, India's bid for metal outside China's reach.

us-10y.standing: The interest rate the US government pays to borrow for ten years, set by trading in its bonds. Mortgages, corporate loans and other governments' debt are priced off it, so it sets the cost of money well beyond America.
us-10y.recent: The Fed left rates unchanged in late October despite inflation, and Warsh's muddled messaging revived doubts about its credibility. Then core consumer prices rose 0.3% in October, Logan called for two more hikes, traders put 78% odds on a December hike, and two-year yields jumped 18 basis points overnight.

sp500.standing: An index of 500 large companies listed on US stock exchanges, weighted by market value. It is the benchmark most pension and index funds are measured against, and a handful of technology firms carry much of its weight.
sp500.recent: The slide came with the midterms: a Democratic sweep and a backlash against data centres hit chipmakers hardest, with Nvidia down 6%, AMD 12% and Micron 11% on Thursday. The AI rout reached Asia a day later, where South Korea halted trading after the Kospi fell 8%.

nasdaq100.standing: The 100 largest non-financial companies listed on the Nasdaq exchange in New York, weighted by size. A handful of technology giants make up most of it, so it reads as the price of American big tech.
nasdaq100.recent: The slide bottomed out in a chip sell-off after the midterms, when a data-centre backlash cut AMD 12% and Micron 11% in a day and the rout spread to Asia. The rebound then stalled on Nvidia: a probe into Jensen Huang knocked it 6.27%, briefly behind Microsoft, and reports the board may oust him sent its futures down nearly 12%.

us-gas-retail.standing: The average price US drivers pay for a gallon of regular gasoline at the pump, taxes included. It follows crude oil and refining costs with a lag, and it is the energy price American households and voters notice most.
us-gas-retail.recent: The pump price still carries the Iran war's oil shock, which priced out enough demand that oil emissions fell 1.9%. The same disruption is paying US refiners: freight to Asia now costs $30-$35 a barrel, Valero says, which leaves crude discounted at home. The US has meanwhile raised its forecasts for 2027 gasoline and diesel prices.

natgas-ttf.standing: The wholesale price of natural gas in Europe, set at the Dutch TTF hub where the continent's pipeline and LNG supplies are traded. Household heating bills, power prices and fertiliser costs across the EU follow it.
natgas-ttf.recent: Gulf LNG now moves through the Hormuz disruption: ADNOC Gas is studying export routes that avoid it, and Qatar's carrier Al Mayeda was struck by unidentified objects in the Gulf. Other buyers of the same cargoes pay too. Pakistan raised its imported gas price by up to 15.27% and rations gas, with nighttime power cuts.

vix.standing: The CBOE Volatility Index: the swing in the S&P 500 over the next 30 days implied by the prices of its options. It rises when investors pay more for protection against a fall, which is why it is called the fear gauge.
vix.recent: None of the fortnight's news pins down the early-November spike. In the background were the war with Iran, which disrupted Hormuz and lifted Aramco's profit, and the Fed's Waller saying he would back at least a quarter-point rate hike in December as US inflation data loomed.

fx-pkr.standing: What one US dollar costs in Pakistani rupees, under a float the State Bank of Pakistan manages. Pakistan pays for its fuel imports in dollars, so a weaker rupee reaches pump prices and household bills.
fx-pkr.recent: Foreign money has been arriving to steady it: UAE investors bought $395.7 million of Pakistan's bonds since July. The import bill it covers stays heavy: even after the latest cut, diesel sells at Rs364 a litre against a pre-war Rs281, and gas rationing and nighttime power cuts persist despite the Hormuz deal.

fx-ngn.standing: Nigeria's currency, quoted as naira per US dollar. Africa's most populous country earns most of its dollars from crude oil and imports much of what it consumes, so the rate sets what fuel and food cost there.
fx-ngn.recent: The fortnight's Nigerian news was about the 2027 contest, with a court voiding Atiku's nomination and 375 tribunal judges sworn in, and about two suspected Ebola cases in the North-east. None of it accounts for the exchange rate.

fx-egp.standing: How many Egyptian pounds buy one US dollar. Egypt imports much of its wheat and fuel and owes heavily in dollars, so a weaker pound feeds straight into food prices and the cost of servicing its debt.
fx-egp.recent: The Suez Canal, one of Egypt's main sources of dollars, earned $724 million in October. That was its highest monthly revenue since 2023 and a 94% jump, despite Houthi threats to shipping in the Red Sea.

fx-try.standing: How many Turkish lira buy one US dollar, so a rising line is a weakening lira. Turkey imports most of its energy and its companies owe heavily in foreign currency, so the rate feeds straight into prices and repayments.
fx-try.recent: Turkey's news in the fortnight was COP31 opening in Antalya, an explosion that killed 16 workers at a Habaş steel plant in Aliağa, and a rift with Azerbaijan that Erdoğan's visit to Shusha patched over. None of it accounts for the currency's price.

fx-bdt.standing: What one US dollar costs in Bangladeshi taka, a rate the central bank manages closely. Garment exports and remittances from workers abroad supply the dollars; fuel, cotton and food imports spend them.
fx-bdt.recent: The news out of Bangladesh in this window was garment workers protesting for days over pay, answered by a new wage board in Dhaka, and Sheikh Hasina applying for a passport in a step toward returning home. Neither story carried anything about the exchange rate or the dollar supply, and neither accounts for the taka's weakening.

fx-idr.standing: How many rupiah one US dollar buys, so a rising line is a weaker currency. Indonesia sells coal, nickel and palm oil in dollars and relies on foreign buyers for its bonds, so it moves with commodity prices and capital flows.
fx-idr.recent: The rupiah slid through a political crisis in Jakarta: three top police officers were arrested for allegedly tapping the president's phone, his chief of staff was dismissed, and 20,980 troops deployed in the capital. A week later Prabowo accepted the resignation of his vice president.

fx-lbp.standing: The price of one US dollar in Lebanese pounds. Lebanon imports most of its food, fuel and medicine and pays for them in dollars, so the rate sets what a salary earned in pounds can buy.
fx-lbp.recent: The fortnight's news from Lebanon was about Israel's war on its land: 24% of wheatland left fallow in the Bekaa Valley, olive groves bulldozed at Kfarshouba, and refugees in Beddawi squeezed by energy prices and inflation. None of it explains the pound's small slip.

fx-cny.standing: How many Chinese yuan one US dollar buys. The central bank sets a daily reference rate and lets trading stray only 2% either side, so the rate is partly policy, and it decides how cheap Chinese exports are abroad.
fx-cny.recent: The yuan's strength bit hardest against the euro, on which it had gained 9%, squeezing margins for exporters in Ningbo. Beijing also widened the currency's reach, letting 19 African countries pay in yuan without New York or London banks, and set its sights on marine insurance; none of this accounts for the move against the dollar.

fx-inr.standing: How many rupees buy one US dollar, so a rising line is a weakening rupee. The Reserve Bank of India manages it loosely, and because India imports most of its oil, a weaker rupee raises fuel prices for 1.4 billion people.
fx-inr.recent: The weeks behind this stretch carried India buying crude from about 43 countries after the Hormuz closure, a ban on black mass exports, and Jio Platforms listing at $137.1 billion; none of it is tied to the rupee's firming against the dollar.

fx-brl.standing: How many Brazilian reais one US dollar buys; a higher number is a weaker real. Brazil exports soy, iron ore and oil and pays high interest rates, so the currency moves on commodity prices and on doubts about public spending.
fx-brl.recent: The real slid after Lula's election win, which Bloomberg framed as the end of the investor class's enthusiasm for him. Brazil's central bank then said inflation had passed the top of its target range as growth slows. It named oil, El Niño, labor and FX shocks, so the weaker currency is itself one of the forces lifting prices.

fx-mxn.standing: The number of Mexican pesos one US dollar buys, so a rising line is a weaker peso. Latin America's most traded currency, it moves on US trade policy and interest rates, because most of Mexico's exports go north.
fx-mxn.recent: Mexico's news over the period was the arrest in Zapopan of Rafael Alvarez, linked to Mayor Carlos Manzo's murder, and the death of Cuauhtémoc Cárdenas at 92; neither bears on the exchange rate.

fx-eur.standing: How many euros one US dollar buys. The euro is shared by most European Union states and is the world's second reserve currency; it moves on the gap between ECB and Federal Reserve interest rates.
fx-eur.recent: Christine Lagarde said she would leave the ECB in February, and 21 euro-area governments had until Friday to nominate her successor. Forecasters meanwhile raised euro zone inflation to 3.0%, reopening debate over a rate hike. Neither event accounts for the euro's moves against the dollar.

fx-jpy.standing: How many yen one US dollar buys, so a rising line is a weaker yen. Japan pays for nearly all its energy in dollars, and its low interest rates have long made the yen the currency the world borrows cheaply.
fx-jpy.recent: Tokyo confirmed it spent a record ¥7.98 trillion buying yen in one day, and the slide resumed anyway. The yen's one clear gain came when the dollar fell and it rose 0.7% alongside the franc. The weak yen let nearly half of Japan's manufacturers raise their profit forecasts.

fx-rub.standing: How many rubles buy one US dollar. Russia earns its foreign currency mostly from oil and gas, and sanctions and capital controls shape the rate, so it moves on energy prices and state policy as much as on trade.
fx-rub.recent: The ruble's strongest day came as an aid convoy entered besieged Oleshky under a Melania Trump-brokered ceasefire, ahead of Trump meeting Kirill Dmitriev at the White House and the first Russia-Ukraine talks in 9 months in Abu Dhabi. Sanctioned Russian crude sold above Brent as China and India bought, bringing in the dollars the ruble trades on.

fx-zar.standing: South Africa's currency, quoted as rand per US dollar, so a rising line means a weaker rand. One of the most traded emerging-market currencies, it moves with the metals the country exports and with global appetite for risk.
fx-zar.recent: The US suspended South Africa's AGOA duty-free access, which carried $1.7 billion of exports in 2025, and local elections left 110 councils projected to hang. Neither pushed the rand off course, and it held steady through hawkish Fed signals.

btc.standing: The dollar price of one bitcoin, the first and largest cryptocurrency, whose supply is capped at 21 million coins. It trades around the clock, and the rest of the crypto market tends to move with it.
btc.recent: Binance lost $6.3 billion to a theft the FBI blamed on North Korea's TraderTraitor, and once withdrawals reopened its customers pulled a net $4.72 billion. The CLARITY Act then stalled 49 to 50 in the Senate, $1.26 billion in leveraged bets were liquidated as tech stocks fell, and spot bitcoin ETFs lost a net $1.282 billion last week.

eth.standing: The token of the Ethereum network, the blockchain most stablecoins, lending protocols and tokenised assets run on. Every transaction there is paid for in it, so its price tracks use of the network as well as appetite for crypto.
eth.recent: Binance lost $6.3 billion in a hack the FBI blamed on North Korea's TraderTraitor, and froze $2.54bn of funds while it covered 90% of the losses; North Korea denied it. Withdrawals resumed, but the selloff spread across crypto, and bitcoin fell below $75,000 for the first time since September 15.

paxg.standing: The dollar price of a troy ounce of gold on New York's COMEX futures market. Gold pays no interest, so it tends to fall when yields and the dollar rise, and central banks and households buy it when they distrust currencies.
paxg.recent: The Democratic sweep in the midterms sent the dollar and Treasury yields down, and December gold futures jumped 3% on the result. Hot US inflation and Fed remarks then turned the market toward a Fed rate hike, which raises the cost of holding a metal that pays nothing. Chinese gold ETFs drew $784 million in October as prices fell.

wiki-russia.standing: How many people open the Wikipedia article on Russia each day. It jumps when the country does something the wider world wants explained, so it marks which events reached people who do not follow the news closely.
wiki-russia.recent: Russia and Ukraine opened their first peace talks in 9 months in Abu Dhabi, where the US pressed for a new security framework covering Europe. Alexander Darchiev, Moscow's ambassador in Washington, died as the talks began, and Ukrainian drones set the Kirishi refinery, Russia's second-largest, ablaze.

wiki-strait-of-hormuz.standing: Daily readers of Wikipedia's article on the channel between Iran and Oman through which Gulf oil and gas reach the open sea. About a fifth of the world's oil passes through it, and no sea route goes around it.
wiki-strait-of-hormuz.recent: US strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island landed as an Iranian commander set out five conditions for regional security. Since then the IRGC says tankers have hit mines and burned on a route Iran bans, Iraq secured its own oil export lane, and Iran claims Oman agreed shipping lanes through the strait.

cp:hormuz.standing: One-fifth of global seaborne oil passes through this 21-mile strait between Iran and Oman.
cp:hormuz.recent: Iran's Revolutionary Guards say tankers struck mines and that the strait stays shut, and Iran says two more burned on a route it had banned. Parliament speaker Ghalibaf claims Oman agreed new shipping lanes, according to TASS; Oman has not confirmed it. Cut off from Gulf barrels, China and India are bidding up Russian crude.

cp:bab-el-mandeb.standing: Between Yemen and Djibouti — the Red Sea’s southern gate. Houthi attacks since 2023 have pushed container shipping to reroute around Africa.
cp:bab-el-mandeb.recent: The strait runs past an open Saudi-Houthi war. Saudi strikes on Yemen have killed or wounded 1,039 people since 13 July, and a Houthi strike on Riyadh's airport killed at least 13 on 10 October. Since then, intercepted missiles damaged Aramco Tower, and an unclaimed attack set ablaze the East-West pipeline that carries Saudi crude to Yanbu.

cp:suez.standing: Egypt’s 120-mile artery carries roughly 12% of global trade. The 2021 closure disrupted supply chains for weeks; Red Sea instability keeps it volatile.
cp:suez.recent: Ships have been coming back. The canal earned $724 million in October, up 94% and its highest monthly revenue since 2023, even with Houthi threats still hanging over the Red Sea. Egypt is also moving off the sidelines in the Saudi-Houthi conflict, which decides whether the southern approach to the canal is safe to sail.

cp:malacca.standing: Between Malaysia and Sumatra — the fastest route between the Indian and Pacific Oceans. Over 80,000 ships a year, including most of China’s oil imports.
cp:malacca.recent: The fortnight's shipping news came from the far end of the Gulf crude route that runs through here: Iran targeted 11 tankers in 10 days in Hormuz by its own media's count, a seafarer died aboard the Velos Sapphire, and Valero put freight to Asia at $30-$35 a barrel. None of it explains the traffic in this strait itself.

cp:taiwan.standing: Between mainland China and Taiwan — roughly 40% of the world’s container traffic passes through, and the flashpoint of any US–China confrontation.
cp:taiwan.recent: The news from the strait was military, not commercial: Taiwan's map tracked 53 Chinese ships, 34 of them warships, along the first island chain. Nothing reported closed or rerouted merchant shipping, and none of it accounts for the count.

cp:panama.standing: 50-mile shortcut between the Atlantic and Pacific. Drought in 2023–24 cut daily transits by half — a live example of climate binding to trade.
cp:panama.recent: The fortnight's news carried nothing about the canal itself. The shipping stories were elsewhere: the Suez Canal's October revenue and Russian strikes on cargo ships off Odesa, and neither accounts for traffic here.

cp:bosporus.standing: Istanbul’s 20-mile waterway links the Black Sea to the Mediterranean — the only route for Russian naval access and Ukrainian grain exports.
cp:bosporus.recent: Drones hit at least 7 Black Sea ships in October and sank the Contship Jet off Bulgaria. Russia then struck three cargo ships at Odesa that it said carried weapons to Ukraine, hitting the Ukrainian grain trade that exits through this strait. Zelensky says Turkey will help restore the grain corridor, and the EU pledged €50 million to a Black Sea security hub.

cp:gibraltar.standing: 8 miles between Morocco and Spain — the only Atlantic–Mediterranean link. A surveillance chokepoint for Russian submarines and sanctioned oil.
cp:gibraltar.recent: Spain's first general strike in 14 years, called over rents rather than wages, took 90% of port workers out, but it began after the latest reading here. Nothing reported in the window accounts for the October trough in traffic.

cp:dover.standing: The busiest shipping lane on Earth — 400+ ships a day squeeze through the English Channel’s 21-mile narrows.
cp:dover.recent: The fortnight's news from either shore was about French wage strikes and street protests, and the supermarket-freezer cyberattack France blamed on Iran's Revolutionary Guards. None of it touched shipping in the English Channel or the ports on it.

cp:cape-of-good-hope.standing: The 3,000-mile detour around southern Africa — the alternative when the Red Sea is closed. The new default for tankers since Houthi attacks began.
cp:cape-of-good-hope.recent: The fortnight's shipping news came from the far end of the tanker trade. Iran's navy and Guards reported mines and fires aboard tankers in Hormuz, a seafarer died on the Velos Sapphire, and Valero put freight to Asia at $30-$35 a barrel. None of it says why fewer ships rounded the Cape.

cp:kerch.standing: Between Crimea and Russia — the only access to the Sea of Azov. A flashpoint since 2014 and contested throughout the Russia–Ukraine war.
cp:kerch.recent: Drones reportedly hit at least 7 Black Sea ships last month, and Russia's defence ministry said the 3 cargo ships it struck off Odesa were carrying weapons to Ukraine. None of those strikes, closures or diversions is placed in the strait itself, so they do not account for the traffic here.

mkt:bist.standing: The 100 largest and most traded companies on Borsa İstanbul, Türkiye's only stock exchange. It is priced in lira, so the level carries the country's inflation as much as its earnings: read the direction, not the number.

mkt:bursa-malaysia.standing: The Kuala Lumpur Composite Index: the 30 largest companies on Bursa Malaysia, the national exchange in Kuala Lumpur. It is the world's largest market for Islamic finance instruments and the centre of the global sukuk trade.
mkt:bursa-malaysia.recent: Malaysian news through these weeks centred on Najib Razak leaving Kajang prison for house arrest after his party crowdfunded his fine, and on a Japan metals maker's plan for a $1.2bn copper foil plant. Neither accounts for the fall in the index.

mkt:idx.standing: Every company listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange in Jakarta, counted in one index. It is the market of the world's largest Muslim-majority country, and commodity producers and banks carry most of its weight.
mkt:idx.recent: A wiretapping scandal ran through Jakarta: three top police officers were arrested for allegedly tapping the president's phone, his chief of staff was dismissed, 20,980 troops deployed, and Prabowo reportedly accepted his vice president's resignation. The index's slide began long before it, and nothing here explains it.

mkt:tse.standing: The Nikkei 225 tracks 225 large companies on the Tokyo Stock Exchange, Japan's main market, weighted by share price. Tokyo is Asia's largest exchange and the first major market to price each trading day.
mkt:tse.recent: An AI-driven tech sell-off knocked 3% off the index in one session and spread across Asia, until South Korea halted trading after the Kospi fell 8%. Nearly half of Japan's manufacturers then raised profit forecasts on the weak yen, and Tokyo spent a record ¥7.98 trillion in one day buying it.

mkt:hkex.standing: The Hang Seng Index tracks the largest and most traded companies on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange. It is where mainland Chinese companies meet foreign capital, and the clearest daily read on sentiment toward China.
mkt:hkex.recent: The fortnight's China stories were mostly about AI: Tencent expanded Hy4 inference tenfold, and Kuaishou's video unit Kling raised about 19.8 billion yuan at a value above its parent. Beijing also moved to curb a yuan rally after a record $938.1 billion trade surplus. None of it accounts for the index's slide.

mkt:sse.standing: The SSE Composite tracks every share listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange, mainland China's main board. Largely closed to foreign investors, it follows domestic policy more than global risk appetite.
mkt:sse.recent: The trough came in a weak October for exporters. New export orders fell to 48.7, and a yuan up 9% on the euro squeezed Ningbo's manufacturers. Third-quarter results split the board, with tech profit up 140% while property lost 53.2 billion yuan. The PBOC then set a weaker fixing to slow the yuan's rise.

mkt:krx.standing: The Korea Composite Stock Price Index: every company on the main board of the Korea Exchange in Seoul, weighted by size. Samsung and SK Hynix dominate it, so it moves with the global semiconductor cycle.
mkt:krx.recent: The slide was the Korean leg of a rout in AI stocks that spread across Asia. On Friday the Kospi fell 8% and South Korea halted trading. An index this heavy in Samsung and SK Hynix holds the AI chip trade almost directly, so the selloff in that trade reached Seoul in full.

mkt:bse.standing: The Sensitive Index: 30 of the largest companies on the Bombay Stock Exchange in Mumbai, India. The exchange is Asia's oldest, founded in 1875, and this index is the benchmark for Indian equities.
mkt:bse.recent: The big Mumbai event was Jio Platforms, which listed 25% above its issue price at $137.1 billion and left Ambani owning India's two most valued firms. Carmakers dispatched an estimated 525,000 cars to dealers in October, led by Maruti's festive stocking. Neither event, on its own, explains the index's climb.

mkt:sgx.standing: The 30 largest and most traded companies on the Singapore Exchange, the main market of Southeast Asia's financial hub. Three banks and regional property groups carry most of its weight, so it moves with interest rates.
mkt:sgx.recent: Singapore's news in these weeks was a vault opened to hold 500 tonnes of foreign central-bank gold, DayOne's filing for a Nasdaq listing, and the USS Theodore Roosevelt's last port call before the Iran war; none of it concerns the banks and property firms that make up the index.

mkt:twse.standing: The Taiwan Stock Exchange's capitalisation-weighted index of every common share listed in Taipei. TSMC alone is roughly a third of it, which makes this the most concentrated major market on the map.
mkt:twse.recent: The trough came with an AI rout that spread to Asian chip stocks, deep enough that South Korea halted trading after the Kospi fell 8%; an index this heavy in TSMC takes that hit directly. The day before, Micron paused work on a $4.5 billion Taiwan plant after workers staged Taiwan's first chip-industry strike.

mkt:asx.standing: The 200 largest companies listed on the Australian Securities Exchange in Sydney, weighted by market value. Mining and banking dominate it, and it is often the first major market to react to Chinese demand data.

mkt:jse.standing: The All Share index covers nearly every company listed on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange, South Africa's main market, weighted by size. It is Africa's largest exchange by far, and the only one with a usable public daily series.
mkt:jse.recent: The US suspended South Africa from AGOA, ending duty-free access for exports worth $1.7 billion in 2025, and local elections left 110 councils projected to hang as the ANC slid. A GDP rebasing also counted illegal miners into mining output. None of it lines up with the index's turns.

mkt:b3.standing: The most traded shares on B3, the São Paulo exchange that is Latin America's largest, weighted by market value. Iron ore, oil and Brazilian interest rates drive it, through the miners, oil producers and banks that dominate it.
mkt:b3.recent: After the presidential runoff, economists raised their 2027 inflation forecast to 4.76% from 4.34% and pencilled in higher interest rates with it, the rates this index trades on. A week later the central bank said inflation had passed the top of its target range while growth slowed, blaming oil, El Niño, labor and FX shocks.

mkt:bmv.standing: The Índice de Precios y Cotizaciones tracks about 35 of the largest, most traded companies on the Bolsa Mexicana de Valores in Mexico City. It is Mexico's benchmark, tightly coupled to US demand and the peso.
mkt:bmv.recent: The weeks behind this rally brought the arrest of a Jalisco cartel leader in Zapopan, the death of Cuauhtémoc Cárdenas and a $573 million quarterly loss at Pemex, and none of it accounts for the climb in Mexico's listed companies.

mkt:byma.standing: The S&P Merval tracks the most traded shares on Bolsas y Mercados Argentinos, Argentina's main exchange. Priced in a peso that has repeatedly lost most of its value, it rises even in bad years; only direction means much.

mkt:tsx.standing: The broad benchmark of the Toronto Stock Exchange, Canada's main market, tracking around 200 of its largest companies by market value. Banks, oil producers and miners dominate it, so it trades like a commodity index.
mkt:tsx.recent: The period carried company news from the index's heaviest sectors: Enbridge's quarterly profit rose on its natural gas businesses, and Barrick Mining filed to take its North American gold assets public. Neither accounts for the index's path.

mkt:nyse.standing: The S&P 500 tracks 500 of the largest companies listed on the New York Stock Exchange and Nasdaq, weighted by market value. It is the largest equity market on earth, and its close sets the tone every other market opens against.
mkt:nyse.recent: Core consumer prices rose 0.3% in October, the Fed's Logan called for two more rate hikes, traders priced 78% odds of a December hike, and two-year Treasury yields jumped 18 basis points. Nvidia fell 6.27% and briefly ceded second place to Microsoft as its board investigated Jensen Huang.

mkt:lse.standing: The 100 largest companies listed on the London Stock Exchange, Britain's main market, ranked by market value. Most of their revenue is earned abroad, so a falling pound tends to push the index up.
mkt:lse.recent: The Bank of England raised rates as it forecast British inflation peaking at 4.9%, and Bailey said a second hike was more likely than not if the war went on. Oil majors sat on Iran war windfall cash even as JP Morgan saw the oil market tip into surplus, and none of the fortnight's news on its own accounts for the index's path.

mkt:xetra.standing: The Deutscher Aktienindex: the 40 largest companies on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange, Germany's main market. It is built on the country's industrial and chemical base, making it Europe's clearest export barometer.
mkt:xetra.recent: The German business news of these weeks was Bundesbank chief Nagel backing a third ECB rate hike in December, and Schaeffler cutting 3,500 jobs, three quarters of them in Germany. Neither accounts for the index's climb.

mkt:euronext-paris.standing: The 40 largest companies listed on Euronext Paris, France's main stock market, weighted by the value of their freely traded shares. Luxury and energy groups dominate it, leaving it unusually exposed to Chinese consumer demand.
mkt:euronext-paris.recent: France's economy shrank 0.1% before Fitch cut its outlook on the country, unions struck for wages, and Mélenchon promised 20,000 supporters nationalisations and a NATO exit. All of it came weeks after the index's October trough, and nothing reported explains that earlier fall.

mkt:euronext-amsterdam.standing: The Amsterdam Exchange index tracks the largest, most traded companies on Euronext Amsterdam, the Dutch market. It is the world's oldest exchange, now carried largely by chip-equipment maker ASML.
mkt:euronext-amsterdam.recent: The fortnight's Dutch news centred on Knot's contest with De Cos to replace Lagarde at the European Central Bank, and on 15,498 Dutch firms queued for grid capacity as data centres crowd out warehouses. None of it accounts for the index's path.

mkt:bme.standing: The 35 most liquid companies on the Bolsa de Madrid, Spain's main stock exchange. Its big banks earn much of their profit in Latin America, so the index moves with both regions.
mkt:bme.recent: Spain's fortnight ran on a high-speed train collision that killed 68 people, then the first general strike in 14 years, called by CCOO and UGT over rents 18 days before the 29 November election. Neither was a story about the banks that dominate this index, and nothing in the news accounts for the price.

mkt:borsa-italiana.standing: The 40 largest, most traded companies on Borsa Italiana in Milan, Italy's main market. Banks and utilities dominate it, making it the market most sensitive to Italian sovereign debt spreads.
mkt:borsa-italiana.recent: Italy's news in this period was a helicopter crash in Bosnia that killed four Italians, nationwide marches over living costs, a hacker leak of Tajani's family details and a hoax that emptied 312 schools. None of it touches the banks and utilities that move this index.

mkt:six.standing: The Swiss Market Index: the 20 largest companies on the SIX Swiss Exchange in Zurich, Switzerland's main market. Nestlé, Roche and Novartis carry it, which makes it defensive when the world turns risk-off.
mkt:six.recent: The franc rose almost 1% against the dollar after the US midterms, and Swiss inflation reached its highest in almost three years, but neither accounts for the index's climb.

mkt:nasdaq-stockholm.standing: The OMX Stockholm 30: the 30 most traded shares on Nasdaq Stockholm, Sweden's main stock exchange. Nordic industrials and telecoms weigh heavily in it, which makes it a useful early read on European capital spending.

mkt:tase.standing: The 125 largest companies by market value on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange, Israel's only stock market. It trades Sunday to Thursday and is heavily weighted to banks, defence and technology.
mkt:tase.recent: The trough came in the week Trump announced an end to $4 billion annual US aid to Israel after 2026, while the election count left no one a majority. Since then 67 of 120 Knesset members have recommended Eisenkot, who has 28 days to build a coalition as Netanyahu stays on as caretaker, still commanding the security services.

wiki-donald-trump.standing: The number of people who open the Wikipedia article on Donald Trump, the US president, each day. It rises when he does something readers want to look up, a rough gauge of how far American politics is reaching a general audience.
wiki-donald-trump.recent: Republicans lost both chambers in the midterms, and Vance said the Iran war was the reason. Trump called the result dishonest, named Stephen Miller chief of staff in place of Wiles, and ordered the Justice Department to investigate Democrats, while Republicans killed a bid to impeach Hegseth.

fed-funds.standing: The range the Federal Reserve sets for overnight lending between US banks. Every dollar borrowing cost is priced off it, from mortgages and Treasury yields to the debts of governments and companies far outside the United States.
fed-funds.recent: The Fed held rates unchanged in October despite inflation, then the data turned against the pause: employers added 165,000 jobs against 65,000 forecast and core prices rose 0.3%. Logan called for two more hikes, traders put 78% odds on a December move, and two-year Treasury yields jumped 18 basis points on fear of a half-point step.

ecb-rate.standing: The interest the European Central Bank pays commercial banks on money parked with it overnight, and the rate that steers borrowing costs across the euro zone. Mortgages, business loans and government bond yields move after it.
ecb-rate.recent: Eurozone inflation hit 4% after eight straight months above 2%, pushed up by the Iran war's oil shock. The ECB held while Panetta and Nagel argued for a December hike. Lagarde leaves on 7 February, so the contest between Knot and De Cos is also a choice between hawk and dove for the rate path.

us-unemployment.standing: The share of the American labour force without a job and actively looking for one, from a monthly household survey. It is one half of the Federal Reserve's mandate, so interest rates move with it.
us-unemployment.recent: US employers added 165,000 jobs in October against 65,000 forecast, and that hiring pace sent Treasuries lower as traders bet the Fed would raise rates again. The Fed's Barkin said the policy direction was clear but needed a careful pace, and the BLS reported that prices rose slightly in October.

xag.standing: The price of a troy ounce of silver on New York's COMEX futures market. It is part precious metal and part industrial input, used in solar panels and electronics, so it moves with gold and with factory demand.
xag.recent: Gold, which silver usually tracks, held near $4,000 as hot US inflation and Fed remarks put a rate hike in view, a weight on metals that pay no yield. China extended its gold-buying streak to two years. None of it explains the slide that began in late summer.

us-cpi.standing: The yearly rise in the Consumer Price Index, the Bureau of Labor Statistics' monthly measure of what American households pay. The Federal Reserve sets interest rates against it, and borrowing costs worldwide follow.
us-cpi.recent: The Fed left rates unchanged in late October despite the pickup. The October CPI report then showed inflation slowing less than expected, and the Fed's Goolsbee called it 'borderline disturbing'. Treasuries slid as traders firmed up bets on a December rate move, and Bitcoin fell to almost a three-month low.

portwatch-hormuz-tanker.standing: A daily count of oil tankers passing the Strait of Hormuz, the narrow channel between Iran and Oman. About a fifth of the world's oil leaves the Gulf through it, so a drop here reaches fuel prices in Asia first.
portwatch-hormuz-tanker.recent: The strait stays shut as Iranian leverage: the Revolutionary Guards say 3 tankers hit mines there, and Rezaei ties reopening to Washington meeting Iran's seven conditions. Iran's media count 11 tankers targeted in 10 days. Ghalibaf claims Oman agreed new shipping lanes, TASS reported; Oman has not confirmed it.

portwatch-bab-container.standing: Container ships crossing the strait between Yemen and Djibouti each day, the southern gate of the Red Sea and the Suez route between Asia and Europe. When it is unsafe, lines divert around Africa and freight takes weeks longer.
portwatch-bab-container.recent: Container ships returning to the route showed up in Egypt's accounts: the Suez Canal earned $724 million in October, double its earlier take. The fortnight's strikes landed inland, with Houthi missiles on Riyadh and the Aramco Tower and an unclaimed attack on Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline.

portwatch-suez-total.standing: The number of ships passing each day through Egypt's canal between the Mediterranean and the Red Sea, the short route between Asia and Europe. When it falls, cargo is going round Africa, adding days and fuel to every voyage.
portwatch-suez-total.recent: Egypt's Suez Canal earned $724 million in October, double its earlier take, on a month of high traffic. The Houthi war has since turned on Saudi Arabia, with strikes on Riyadh, Aramco Tower and the East-West pipeline, but nothing reported links it to ships avoiding the canal.

portwatch-panama-total.standing: Ships crossing the Panama Canal each day, the shortcut between the Atlantic and the Pacific. Its locks run on fresh water from Gatún Lake, so drought in Panama cuts the daily slots and delays trade between Asia and the US east coast.

portwatch-malacca-total.standing: The count of ships passing each day through the strait between Malaysia and Indonesia's Sumatra, the shortest sea route from the Indian Ocean to the Pacific. Most oil East Asia imports from the Middle East goes through it.
portwatch-malacca-total.recent: Much of the crude Asia buys reaches Malacca by way of Hormuz, where Iran says it targeted 11 tankers in 10 days, and where Iran and Iraq each claim lanes agreed with Oman. China still imported nearly 42 million tons of crude in October. None of it accounts for the strait's own traffic.

portwatch-taiwan-total.standing: The count of cargo ships and tankers passing each day between Taiwan and mainland China. The strait is the main lane between the ports of north-east Asia and the routes south, and typhoons and military drills both empty it.

portwatch-dover-total.standing: The narrowest part of the English Channel, between England and France, and one of the busiest shipping lanes in the world. Most cargo sailing between the Atlantic and the ports of northern Europe passes through it.
portwatch-dover-total.recent: Nothing reported in the fortnight explains the swing in Dover Strait traffic. The news from France was wage strikes, a fourth weekend of protests, and prosecutors blaming Iran's Revolutionary Guards for heating freezers in 700 French supermarkets. None of it touched shipping.

portwatch-gibraltar-total.standing: The count of ships passing each day through the 14-kilometre gap between Spain and Morocco, the only sea route between the Atlantic and the Mediterranean. Traffic bound to or from the Suez Canal passes here too.

wiki-ukraine.standing: How many times a day Wikipedia's article on Ukraine is opened. Readers arrive when the country's war with Russia, its grain exports or its diplomacy turn up in the news, so the count marks when the world looks its way.
wiki-ukraine.recent: Russia, Ukraine and the US met in Abu Dhabi on 10 November for the first peace talks in 9 months. A US official floated NATO-like guarantees for Ukraine, and the US called for a new security framework covering Europe. Days earlier, Russian strikes left about 850,000 people without power in Dnipropetrovsk and hit 3 cargo ships off Odesa.

xmr.standing: A cryptocurrency built to hide the sender, receiver and amount of every transaction. That privacy makes it the coin of choice for ransomware crews and darknet markets, and the one exchanges delist under regulatory pressure.

co:nvidia.standing: Designs the processors that most artificial-intelligence models are trained and run on, and sells them to the companies building data centres. It designs chips and does not make them: TSMC does.
co:nvidia.recent: US officials reportedly believe Chinese intelligence targeted Jensen Huang through Megaspeed's Alice Huang, whose employer bought $4.8bn of Nvidia equipment. The board opened an inquiry, Sen. Cramer called on him to resign, and reports that the board may oust him sent Nvidia futures lower.

co:apple.standing: Makes the iPhone, which brings in about half its sales, along with Mac computers, iPads and watches, and takes a cut of what is sold through its App Store.
co:apple.recent: Apple reported a record quarter carried by India, but its new CEO called memory chip prices "unprecedented", guided gross margin to 45-46% from 47.9% and raised prices, and the shares shed about $140 billion after hours. In China, Siri's AI now runs on Alibaba's Qwen, and a touchscreen MacBook Pro reached reviewers.

co:alphabet.standing: Owns Google and YouTube. Most of its money comes from advertising beside search results and videos; it also sells cloud computing and builds its own AI models.
co:alphabet.recent: Alphabet's quarter showed capital spending up 114% to $51.4 billion, enough to turn its cash flow negative while search fell short. The spending on AI has continued since: Google is buying $10 billion of Anthropic in its IPO, and can take over Anthropic's $19 billion data center lease.

co:amazon.standing: An online retailer, and through Amazon Web Services the largest seller of cloud computing, which earns most of its profit.
co:amazon.recent: The trough came with Amazon's quarterly results. They showed that spending on AI had pushed its 12-month cash burn to a record $42.4 billion, as tech earnings deflated enthusiasm for AI across big tech. Nothing reported since then about the company's own business accounts for the recovery that followed.

co:tsmc.standing: Manufactures the chips other companies design, among them Apple’s, Nvidia’s and AMD’s, and makes most of the world’s most advanced ones, in Taiwan.

co:microsoft.standing: Sells Windows and Office, and rents out computing power through Azure, one of the largest clouds. It holds a large stake in OpenAI.
co:microsoft.recent: Kaspersky found the BlackX bootkit infecting fully patched Windows machines, PC revenue slid, and OpenAI, in which Microsoft holds a stake, raised $11 billion at $1.25 trillion, below the $1.4 trillion it first sought. None of it accounts for the share price. Microsoft briefly passed Nvidia in market cap only because Nvidia fell.

co:broadcom.standing: Makes the networking chips that connect data centres and designs custom AI chips for companies such as Google. It also owns the software firm VMware.
co:broadcom.recent: Anthropic's S-1, the filing that opens a company's books ahead of a stock-market listing, was read as strengthening the case for Broadcom's AI growth, because its custom-chip business depends on a handful of AI developers. Nothing in the fortnight's news accounts for the slide that came before it.

co:spacex.standing: Builds reusable rockets, launches satellites and astronauts for governments and companies, and runs Starlink, a satellite internet network.
co:spacex.recent: The slide came the week SpaceX's default risk hit a fresh peak in a tech-led selloff, and as Musk's political bet failed, raising questions over his Tesla, SpaceX and China ties. SpaceX was also weighing a merger with Tesla, which Barclays called a key part of the Tesla bull case.

co:meta.standing: Owns Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp, used by more than three billion people, and earns nearly all its money from advertising on them.
co:meta.recent: The fortnight brought Meta a fine from Brazil's electoral court for nine days of missed takedown orders, a retreat from terms claiming AI training rights over customers' websites, and preparations for a cross-border investment-grade bond sale. None of it accounts for the share price.

co:aramco.standing: Saudi Arabia’s state oil company, which pumps more oil than any other company. The government owns nearly all of it, and its dividends pay for much of the kingdom’s budget.
co:aramco.recent: Aramco's third-quarter profit rose 9% to $31.2 billion on oil prices lifted by the Hormuz crisis, and it began widening the East-West pipeline that carries crude around the strait. Then the war reached it: Houthis claimed six strikes in the kingdom, debris damaged Aramco Tower in Riyadh, and an attack set the pipeline ablaze.

co:tesla.standing: Makes electric cars, and the batteries that store power for homes and electricity grids. Led by Elon Musk, who also leads SpaceX.
co:tesla.recent: Tesla said it would stop building the Cybertruck, which sold 11,586 units in nine months by Cox Automotive's estimate, as Musk turns the company toward robotics and AI; the shares jumped 4% that morning. Days later it claimed its steering-wheel-free Cybercab meets federal safety standards, without explaining how.

co:samsung.standing: One of the three companies that make most of the world’s memory chips, and one of the largest makers of smartphones and televisions.
co:samsung.recent: Samsung's quarterly results, released alongside Alphabet's, rattled technology shares. The same week it was reported to be ending fridge and washing-machine sales in Hong Kong, and days later Samsung joined Tesla in opposing new US tariffs on Vietnam, where it builds much of what it sells.

co:micron.standing: The one large American maker of memory chips, the kind that hold data in phones, computers and AI data centres. Its two main rivals are Samsung and SK Hynix.
co:micron.recent: About 12 Micron workers in Taoyuan staged Taiwan's first chip-industry strike, and the company paused work on its $4.5 billion Taiwan plant over the labor spat. That came on the same Thursday chip makers sold off together after the midterms, so the stock took a blow of its own on top of the sector-wide one.

co:amd.standing: Designs processors for computers and data centres, where it competes with Intel, and AI chips, where it competes with Nvidia. Like Nvidia, it has TSMC make them.
co:amd.recent: AMD's forecast beat estimates as data-center revenue jumped 97% to $8.55 billion, even as its gaming sales cratered. Two days later chipmakers sold off after the midterms, AMD by 12% against Nvidia's 6%, on a backlash against data centres, the very business carrying its growth.

co:berkshire.standing: A holding company built by Warren Buffett. It owns insurers, a railway and energy utilities outright, and holds large stakes in companies such as Apple and Coca-Cola.

co:lilly.standing: An American drugmaker. Its diabetes and weight-loss medicines, sold as Mounjaro and Zepbound, account for much of its growth.

co:jpmorgan.standing: The largest bank in the United States by assets, serving households, companies and governments.

co:skhynix.standing: A South Korean maker of memory chips, and the main supplier of the high-speed memory that Nvidia’s AI chips need.

co:walmart.standing: The world’s largest retailer by sales, with thousands of stores in the United States and abroad.
co:walmart.recent: Walmart joined Eli Lilly and 36 other issuers in objecting to OKX and ICE trading tokenized versions of their shares. Neither that dispute nor DoorDash's $17 billion purchase of Instacart, a delivery rival, accounts for the share price.

co:asml.standing: A Dutch company, and the only maker of the machines needed to print the most advanced chips. Every leading chipmaker buys from it, and its sales to China are restricted.

us-2y.standing: The interest rate the US government pays to borrow for two years. Of all Treasury yields it follows the Federal Reserve's policy rate most closely, so it shows where traders are betting that rate goes next.

us-mortgage.standing: The average interest rate US lenders charge on a 30-year fixed home loan, the mortgage most American buyers take. It follows long-dated Treasury yields, and it sets what a house costs each month and whether owners can afford to move.

ez-cpi.standing: The annual rise in consumer prices across the countries that share the euro, measured by Eurostat on one harmonised basket. The European Central Bank aims for 2% and sets the bloc's interest rates against it.
ez-cpi.recent: October came in at 4%, the eighth straight month above 2%, and forecasters now expect the year to average 3.0%, which has opened a debate at the ECB over raising rates. Nothing in these reports says what is driving prices up.

bnb.standing: The native token of BNB Chain, the blockchain network built by the exchange Binance. Holders use it to pay transaction fees on the chain and get trading discounts on Binance, so its price follows the exchange's fortunes and its regulators.

trx.standing: The token of the Tron blockchain, a network built for cheap, fast transfers. Most of its traffic is the dollar stablecoin Tether, so its price follows demand for moving dollars outside banks, especially in emerging markets.

sol.standing: The token of the Solana blockchain, used to pay its transaction fees and staked by the validators that secure it. Its price is a bet on how much trading and payment traffic the network wins, and it swings harder than Bitcoin.
sol.recent: The fortnight's one Solana-specific story pointed the other way: Schroders, a $1.1 trillion manager, tokenized an emerging-market bond fund on the chain. Nothing else in the input concerns Solana, and none of it accounts for the token's fall.

xrp.standing: The native token of the XRP Ledger, a payments network built for fast cross-border transfers. Ripple, the company most closely tied to it, holds a large share of the supply, so its legal and commercial fortunes move the price.
xrp.recent: XRP fell with the rest of crypto. A Binance hack knocked bitcoin and ether, a drop below $80,000 liquidated $356 million in long bets, and an Nvidia-led tech selloff and ETF outflows ahead of U.S. CPI data followed. The XRP Ledger was also set to fix a flaw that could let stablecoin partners print new tokens.

hype.standing: The token of Hyperliquid, a blockchain built to run a derivatives exchange where traders bet on crypto prices with leverage. Trading fees fund buybacks of the token, so its price follows how much business the exchange does.
hype.recent: Hyperliquid's perpetual contracts became where traders took 10-fold leveraged bets on Anthropic's initial public offering, and where Nvidia futures fell first on reports the board may oust Jensen Huang. Neither story accounts for the token's own slide.

doge.standing: A cryptocurrency launched as a joke around a Shiba Inu dog meme, with no cap on how many coins can exist. It has little use beyond payments and tipping, so its price moves on online attention and celebrity endorsement.

zec.standing: A cryptocurrency built on Bitcoin's design, with the same 21 million coin cap, that lets users hide sender, receiver and amount using zero-knowledge proofs. It is the main market price put on financial privacy on a public blockchain.
zec.recent: Zcash jumped 12% on 5 November in a post-election crypto rebound that kept Bitcoin above $80,000. No reporting since then explains the slide that followed.

boe-rate.standing: Bank Rate, the interest the Bank of England pays commercial banks on their reserves, set by its nine-member Monetary Policy Committee. British mortgage, savings and business loan rates are priced off it, and sterling moves with it.
boe-rate.recent: This monthly reading predates the Bank of England's unanimous hike on 5 November, its first rise since 2023, which ended the run of cuts. The Bank now forecasts inflation peaking at 4.9%, and Bailey said a second hike was more likely than not if the war goes on.

link.standing: The token of Chainlink, a network of oracles that feeds outside data such as prices into blockchain smart contracts. Node operators are paid in it, and much of decentralised lending relies on its price feeds.

boj-rate.standing: The Bank of Japan's short-term policy rate, the price of overnight money in yen. Kept near zero for decades, it made the yen the world's cheapest currency to borrow, so a rise pulls money back to Japan from markets everywhere.
boj-rate.recent: Ueda said the 2% inflation goal was not yet sustainably achieved, then a week later saw 'some upside risks', and wholesale inflation accelerated after that. The pressure runs both ways: Japan spent a record ¥7.98 trillion in one day buying yen, while Uniqlo reversed a sock price rise within days as shoppers balked.

tcmb-rate.standing: The one-week repo rate at which the Central Bank of the Republic of Türkiye lends to commercial banks, and the country's main policy rate. It sets the cost of lira credit and shapes how attractive the currency is to hold against inflation.

pboc-rate.standing: The one-year loan prime rate, the benchmark the People's Bank of China steers and that banks use to price most new business and household loans. It sets the cost of credit across the world's second-largest economy.
pboc-rate.recent: The People's Bank of China's moves this fortnight were about the currency, not the cost of credit. It set a weaker yuan fixing and raised the forex deposit reserve requirement to slow a yuan rally fed by a record trade surplus, and none of that touched its lending rate.

bcb-rate.standing: The Selic, the overnight rate the Central Bank of Brazil sets to steer inflation toward its target. It prices government debt and bank lending across Latin America's largest economy, and the real's appeal to foreign money rises and falls with it.
bcb-rate.recent: Brazil's central bank is caught between two pressures: inflation has passed the top of its target range while growth slows. The bank names four separate shocks behind the overshoot, so it cannot ease to support a cooling economy without letting prices run further.

bi-rate.standing: The rate Bank Indonesia sets for seven-day lending to commercial banks, its main policy tool. It steers borrowing costs across Southeast Asia's largest economy and is used to defend the rupiah when capital flows out.

cbr-rate.standing: The Bank of Russia's key rate, the price at which it lends to and takes deposits from commercial banks for a week. Rouble mortgages, company loans and the government's own borrowing costs are all priced off it.
cbr-rate.recent: The Bank of Russia raised the path it projects for the key rate, putting fourth-quarter inflation at 7.1-7.6%, and said that higher trajectory is what brings inflation to 4% in 2027. Alongside it, the central bank kept buying yuan on the domestic market, around $150 mln per settlement, while Russia's international reserves fell 1.48% in October.

mkt:set.standing: A capitalisation-weighted index of every common stock on the Stock Exchange of Thailand in Bangkok, the country's main market. It is sensitive to tourism flows and regional energy prices.
mkt:set.recent: Thai inflation hit 3.9%, above the central bank's ceiling. Separately, the closure of the Strait of Hormuz has kept Siam Cement's core Vietnam plastics plant shut until mid-2027 while the company moves its feedstock away from Middle East naphtha.

mkt:tadawul.standing: The Tadawul All Share Index covers every company on the Saudi Exchange's main market in Riyadh, the Arab world's largest by value and dominated by Aramco. It trades Sunday to Thursday, opening the global week before Tokyo.
mkt:tadawul.recent: Aramco, which dominates the index, earned $31.2 billion in the third quarter from the Hormuz crisis, and Saudi output rose 26% in October. Then Houthi missile debris damaged Aramco Tower in Riyadh and an attack set ablaze the East-West pipeline, the export route around Hormuz. The Qatar PM called US talks on Iran positive.

mkt:dfm.standing: The main index of the Dubai Financial Market, the stock exchange in Dubai, United Arab Emirates. It is the Gulf's main listing venue for property and banking, and trades Monday to Friday, unlike Riyadh.
mkt:dfm.recent: The latest leg up came after Trump signalled that new Iran strikes were unnecessary following a Qatar meeting, easing the war risk that had closed Hormuz and brought maritime incidents off the UAE coast. Gulf trade had already adapted to the rerouting: AD Ports reported quarterly profit up 73%, and pipelines were carrying cargo around the strait.

mkt:pse.standing: The PSEi tracks 30 large companies listed on the Philippine Stock Exchange in Manila, the country's only bourse. It is a small, domestically driven market, and remittance flows from Filipinos working abroad move the index.
mkt:pse.recent: The economy under the index lost pace: growth slowed to 2.1% in Q3, dragged by inflation, and businesses were struggling to keep customers through a weak peso and high inflation. Philippine bonds were rated the most exposed in emerging Asia to Fed hikes.

stocks:META.standing: The owner of Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp, which earns nearly all its revenue selling ads to reach more than three billion daily users. Its spending on AI data centres is among the heaviest in the industry.
stocks:META.recent: Meta readied a cross-border investment-grade bond sale to fund AI, shelved terms claiming training rights over its customers' websites after a backlash, and made Dina Powell McCormick, chosen for ties to the Trump administration, president to push data-centre and power projects through permitting. None of these accounts for the share price.

poly-will-pedro-sanchez-be-the-next-prim.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Pedro Sánchez, Spain's Socialist prime minister, heads the government formed after the next general election. The price is what traders pay for a yes, and it moves on polls, coalition arithmetic and court cases.

stocks:0700.HK.standing: The Shenzhen company behind WeChat, the app most of China uses to message and pay, and the world's largest video-game publisher by revenue. Its Hong Kong share is one of the heaviest weights in the Hang Seng index.
stocks:0700.HK.recent: Tencent's news through the fortnight was about AI. It previewed its Hunyuan Hy4 model, then said demand for WorkBuddy had pushed it to expand Hy4 inference capacity tenfold. It followed with an AI search engine that indexes WeChat accounts, turning its own messaging platform into a search corpus no rival can reach.

stocks:NVDA.standing: The American designer of the graphics processors that train and run most of the world's AI models. Data-centre chips earn most of its revenue, so its share price is read as a gauge of what the industry spends on AI.
stocks:NVDA.recent: US officials said Chinese intelligence targeted Jensen Huang through Alice Huang of Megaspeed, a firm reported to have bought $4.8bn of Nvidia equipment. The board opened its own investigation, House committees asked for a closed briefing on 18 November, Sen. Cramer called on him to resign, and reports said the board was weighing his removal.

poly-will-rebeca-grynspan-be-the-next-se.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Rebeca Grynspan, the Costa Rican economist heading UN Trade and Development, becomes the next UN Secretary-General. The Security Council's five veto holders must all accept the nominee.

poly-edi-rama-out-as-albania-pm-in-2026.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Edi Rama stops being Albania's prime minister before the end of 2026. Rama, leader of the Socialist Party, took office in 2013.

poly-trump-putin-and-xi-seen-together-be.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the US, Russian and Chinese leaders meet together in person before 2027. A three-way meeting would put Beijing at the table on matters Washington and Moscow usually settle between themselves.
poly-trump-putin-and-xi-seen-together-be.recent: Nothing in the past fortnight's news points to a three-way meeting with Xi. The nearest thread is the US-brokered talks between Russia and Ukraine in Abu Dhabi, where a US official floated NATO-like guarantees for Ukraine. TASS wrote that Putin is not ready to make peace there.

poly-ex-cuba-leader-raul-castro-in-us-cu.standing: A Polymarket contract paying out if Raúl Castro, Fidel's brother, Cuba's president from 2008 to 2018 and party chief until 2021, is in US custody by year's end. Traders bet on Washington getting him before an American court.

stocks:GOOGL.standing: The parent company of Google, earning most of its revenue from search and YouTube advertising, alongside Google Cloud and Waymo. Its share is a running bet on whether AI assistants strengthen or erode the search ad business.
stocks:GOOGL.recent: The slide began with the quarter's results: search revenue missed, capex jumped 114% to $51.4 billion and free cash flow turned negative, and Google conceded that AI search makes less money. It has kept committing since, buying $10 billion of Anthropic and backstopping Anthropic's $19 billion data center lease with TeraWulf.

poly-saudi-houthi-ceasefire-agreement-an.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Saudi Arabia and Yemen's Houthis agree a ceasefire before the year ends. Its price is what traders pay for a yes, and it moves with strikes, mediation and the Red Sea shipping the war hangs over.
poly-saudi-houthi-ceasefire-agreement-an.recent: The fortnight brought escalation, not talks: Houthis claimed strikes inside the kingdom, missile debris blew out windows across Aramco Tower in Riyadh, an unclaimed attack set the East-West pipeline ablaze, and Saudi strikes on Sanaa killed 27 villagers. Syrian military trainers are now working inside Saudi Arabia.

poly-will-a-us-iran-deal-in-2026-include.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether a US-Iran agreement reached in 2026 has Iran hand over its stockpile of enriched uranium, the material at the centre of the nuclear dispute and of any settlement between the two.
poly-will-a-us-iran-deal-in-2026-include.recent: Tehran denied holding any talks with Washington. Rezaei set seven conditions, got no answer and tied reopening the Strait of Hormuz to one, while Trump held off strikes at the request of Gulf neighbours. None of it touches uranium or accounts for the price.

poly-will-deepseek-ipo-by-december-31-20.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if DeepSeek, the Hangzhou AI lab spun out of the hedge fund High-Flyer, lists its shares before 2028. A listing would open China's most closely watched AI lab to public shareholders.

poly-venezuela-election-scheduled-by-dec.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Venezuela's authorities formally schedule a national election before the end of 2026. Its price is what traders will stake on a vote being called, not on one being held.

poly-will-any-country-join-the-mecca-agr.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if any further country formally joins the Mecca Agreement before the end of 2026. Its price is what traders will stake on the pact widening beyond its founding signatories.

poly-will-peter-obi-win-the-2027-nigeria.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Peter Obi, the former Anambra governor who ran third in 2023, wins Nigeria's presidency in 2027. Its price is what traders will pay on an opposition upset of the ruling APC.

poly-netanyahu-out-before-2027-684-719-2.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Benjamin Netanyahu stops being Israel's prime minister before 2027. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves with coalition crises, court cases and election timing.

poly-sudan-civil-war-ceasefire-by-decemb.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Sudan's army and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces agree a ceasefire before 2026 ends. The war, fought since April 2023, has driven the world's largest displacement crisis.

poly-russia-x-ukraine-ceasefire-agreemen.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Russia and Ukraine agree a ceasefire by the end of November 2026. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves with each round of talks and each wave of strikes.
poly-russia-x-ukraine-ceasefire-agreemen.recent: Russia and Ukraine opened their first peace talks in 9 months in Abu Dhabi on 10 November, but the US steered them toward a security framework for Europe, and TASS ran the line that Putin is not ready to make peace. The Oleshky ceasefire covered one town, and Russian strikes still left 850,000 without power.

poly-russia-x-ukraine-ceasefire-agreemen.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Russia and Ukraine agree a ceasefire before the end of 2026. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves on talks, envoys and sanctions decisions.
poly-russia-x-ukraine-ceasefire-agreemen.recent: Russia and Ukraine held their first talks in 9 months in Abu Dhabi on 10 November. There the US pressed a new security framework covering Europe, which the EU had already rebuffed. Russian strikes on Odesa shipping and the Dnipropetrovsk grid continued around the talks, and TASS reported that Putin is not ready to make peace in Abu Dhabi.

stocks:AAPL.standing: Shares of the Cupertino maker of the iPhone, Mac and iPad, one of the world's most valuable listed companies. The iPhone earns most of its revenue, and its products are assembled largely in China on chips made in Taiwan.
stocks:AAPL.recent: The results showed a record quarter, with India key to iPhone revenue, but the new CEO called memory prices "unprecedented", guided gross margin to 45-46%, down from 47.9%, and raised prices; about $140 billion went in after-hours trading. In China, Alibaba's Qwen now runs the AI behind Siri on iPhones.

poly-will-no-qualifying-diplomatic-us-ir.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if no senior American and Iranian officials meet before 2026 ends. The two governments have met at that level only rarely since 1979, so a meeting would break a long pattern.
poly-will-no-qualifying-diplomatic-us-ir.recent: Tehran says there are no talks: Rezaei set seven conditions Washington has not answered, and now ties reopening the Strait of Hormuz to that answer after three tankers hit mines. Trump held off strikes when Gulf neighbours asked, but Bessent was moved to a military base over Iranian threats against US officials.

poly-openai-1t-valuation-in-2026.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether OpenAI, the maker of ChatGPT, reaches a valuation of at least $1 trillion in 2026. OpenAI is privately held, so this is a rare public wager on what the AI boom's best-known lab is worth.

poly-moodys-or-sp-downgrades-france-by-n.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Moody's or S&P cuts France's sovereign credit rating before its deadline. Those ratings feed into what Paris pays to borrow and which funds can hold its bonds.

poly-will-gyanesh-kumar-be-out-as-chief-.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Gyanesh Kumar leaves office as India's Chief Election Commissioner by the deadline. The post runs national and state votes, and removal requires the same process as for a Supreme Court judge.
poly-will-gyanesh-kumar-be-out-as-chief-.recent: The pressure on him came from the street: thousands joined the INDIA bloc's 'Chalo Dilli' march in Delhi demanding the election chief resign over alleged bias in the electoral rolls, and Ashok Gehlot accused authorities of suppressing dissent ahead of the rally. Nothing in the news since records a resignation or a move to remove him.

poly-will-helen-zille-be-the-next-mayor-.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Helen Zille, the former Cape Town mayor and Western Cape premier, becomes Johannesburg's next mayor. The city council elects the mayor, so coalition deals can matter as much as the vote.

poly-will-iran-withdraw-from-the-npt-bef.standing: A Polymarket contract on Iran formally quitting the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty by 2027. The treaty lets a member leave on three months' notice, and leaving would end the legal basis for inspections of Iran's sites.
poly-will-iran-withdraw-from-the-npt-bef.recent: None of the fortnight's news touched the treaty itself. Tehran's leverage ran through Hormuz instead: Rezaei tied reopening the strait to Washington's answer on Iran's seven conditions, and Trump held off strikes after Gulf neighbours asked him to hold fire.

poly-will-the-us-invade-iran-before-2027.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if U.S. forces invade Iran before 2027; its price is what traders will pay for that outcome. It asks about an invasion, a far higher bar than an air or missile strike.
poly-will-the-us-invade-iran-before-2027.recent: Vance blamed the Iran war for the Republicans' midterm defeat, and Trump then held strikes on Iran after Gulf neighbours asked him to hold fire. Brent fell to a 10-week low as strikes looked unlikely, even as Rezaei kept Hormuz shut until Washington answers Iran's seven conditions and three tankers hit mines there.

poly-us-announces-end-of-iranian-blockad.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the United States ends its blockade of Iran by the close of 2026. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, which is tied to whether Gulf oil reaches its importers.
poly-us-announces-end-of-iranian-blockad.recent: Tehran hardened its terms: Rezaei denied any talks with Washington, set seven conditions, and then tied reopening Hormuz itself to the US answer after the Revolutionary Guards said three tankers hit mines in the strait. In the same week, Iran-linked threats moved Bessent onto a military base.

poly-israel-x-hamas-ceasefire-cancelled-.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the Israel-Hamas ceasefire is cancelled by Dec 31. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it reacts to fighting in Gaza and to the politics of the governments behind the truce.
poly-israel-x-hamas-ceasefire-cancelled-.recent: Gadi Eisenkot gathered the recommendations of 67 of 120 Knesset members to form Israel's next government, then wrote to caretaker prime minister Netanyahu warning him against military or security operations without an immediate threat. Eisenkot has said Israel should not return to war for now.

poly-us-iran-hormuz-agreement-by-decembe.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether the United States and Iran reach an agreement on the Strait of Hormuz by December 31. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, on a waterway that Gulf energy exporters and importers depend on.
poly-us-iran-hormuz-agreement-by-decembe.recent: Tehran's Hormuz diplomacy ran through Oman, not Washington: Ghalibaf claimed, via TASS, a lane deal with Muscat that Oman has not confirmed. Rezaei tied reopening the strait to Washington's answer on seven conditions after the Revolutionary Guards said 3 tankers hit mines there.

poly-will-the-fed-increase-interest-rate.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether the Federal Reserve raises its policy rate by a quarter point at its December meeting. That rate anchors short-term dollar borrowing, so bonds, mortgages and currencies worldwide reprice around it.
poly-will-the-fed-increase-interest-rate.recent: Core consumer prices rose 0.3% in October, and the Fed's Logan answered by calling for two more rate hikes, possibly rapidly, as Waller and other Fed speakers turned hawkish. Two-year Treasury yields jumped 18 basis points overnight, and bets began to price a half-point move rather than a quarter.

poly-us-iran-hormuz-agreement-by-novembe.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Washington and Tehran reach an agreement on the Strait of Hormuz by November 30. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, on the waterway that carries Gulf oil and gas to the world.
poly-us-iran-hormuz-agreement-by-novembe.recent: Tehran turned to Oman rather than Washington. Iran says Muscat agreed the shipping lanes, a claim carried by TASS that Oman has not confirmed. Rezaei tied reopening the strait to Washington's answer on Iran's conditions after the Revolutionary Guards said three tankers hit mines, and Bessent was moved to a military base after threats.

wiki-binance.standing: The Wikipedia article on Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange by trading volume. Millions of retail traders hold funds on it, and much of the market's stablecoin and token liquidity clears through its order books.
wiki-binance.recent: Thieves took $6.3 billion from Binance through malicious code planted via a fake job interview, and the exchange froze $2.54bn in funds while it searched. The FBI blamed North Korea's TraderTraitor, which Kim Yo-jong denied; Binance said it refilled 90% of the loss, and customers withdrew a net $4.72 billion once withdrawals reopened.

stocks:688036.SS.standing: The Shenzhen maker of Tecno, Itel and Infinix phones, sold cheaply across Africa, South Asia and the Middle East. Thin margins on low-priced handsets leave it exposed to the cost of the chips inside them.
stocks:688036.SS.recent: Memory now exceeds 60% of the parts cost of a sub-$100 phone, the segment Transsion is built on, and IDC puts it at 40-50% of a low-end handset's cost across niche makers. That squeeze runs against the share's rise, and nothing reported in the fortnight about Transsion accounts for it.

poly-strait-of-hormuz-traffic-returns-to.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if shipping through the Strait of Hormuz returns to normal by December 31. Roughly a fifth of the world's oil passes the strait, so the price is a bet on Gulf supply reopening.
poly-strait-of-hormuz-traffic-returns-to.recent: Iran's media said it had targeted 11 tankers in 10 days, and the Revolutionary Guards then said 3 more hit mines, with Rezaei tying any reopening to Washington's answer on Iran's seven conditions. Ghalibaf's claim, via TASS, that Oman had agreed the lanes came with his line that the strait will not return to what it was before the war.

stocks:GS.standing: The share price of Goldman Sachs, the New York investment bank listed on the NYSE. Its earnings ride on mergers, share issuance and trading volumes, so the stock tends to track how busy Wall Street's dealmaking is.

poly-will-ukraine-sign-an-eu-accession-t.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Ukraine signs its EU accession treaty by 2027. Signing comes only after every negotiating chapter closes and all 27 member states agree, so the price is a bet on the pace of talks in Brussels.
poly-will-ukraine-sign-an-eu-accession-t.recent: The fortnight's news on Ukraine centred on US-brokered talks with Russia in Abu Dhabi, a US call for a new security framework covering Europe, and EU money for Black Sea security; none of it touched accession or accounts for the contract's price.

poly-pete-hegseth-out-as-secretary-of-de.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Pete Hegseth stops being the US Secretary of Defense before the end of the year. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves on reports about his standing at the Pentagon.

wiki-inflation.standing: The general rise in prices across an economy, usually measured by a consumer price index. Central banks set interest rates to keep it near a target, so its pace decides what borrowers and savers pay.
wiki-inflation.recent: Prices are climbing on several continents at once. The Bank of England raised rates and forecast inflation peaking at 4.9%, eurozone inflation hit 4%, and China's producer prices reached their highest since June 2022. In the US, core prices rose 0.3% in October and the Fed's Logan called for two more rate hikes.

stocks:SHEL.standing: One of the world's largest oil and gas companies, headquartered in London, and the biggest trader of liquefied natural gas. Its profits track crude and gas prices, and its dividend is a fixture of British pension funds.

stocks:DBK.DE.standing: Germany's largest bank, listed in Frankfurt, with an investment bank that earns a large share of its revenue. Its shares move with euro-area interest rates, legal costs and the health of the German industry it lends to.

stocks:002594.SZ.standing: The Shenzhen-listed shares of BYD, China's biggest seller of electric and plug-in hybrid cars. It makes its own batteries, so the same stock carries both its car margins and China's battery business.
stocks:002594.SZ.recent: BYD's Yangwang U9X reached 503.17 km/h on a closed highway in Abu Dhabi, a record for a production car. Separately, Chinese brands now supply 88.4% of Argentina's electric cars. Neither is a result, an order or a ruling that accounts for the share price.
